text:
jordan: quick heads-up — PR #54231 modifies routing fallback for low-capacity model pools. I want to get merge sign-off from runtime (kernel path), platform (routing policy), infra (kv/cache impact), and security (auth header ordering). target merge: Thu 10:00 PT unless any hard blockers. PTAL?

mira: can you paste the small config snippet and the rollout plan? helps me check the platform-side config flags quickly.

jordan: sure — snippet below. the change adds a policy that prefers cheaper model variants when latency SLOs are met, with explicit region fallback.
```yaml
routing:
  policy: pref_cost_with_latency_guard
  fallbacks:
    - model: gptx-compact-8bit
      region: us-west1
    - model: gptx-quant-4bit
      region: us-west1
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  canary_percentage: 10
```

jordan: canary plan: 10% traffic for 2h in us-west1, monitor token latency and error rate. rollback is immediate to previous policy.

sam: runtime note — the kernel selection tweak is tiny but touches the attention kernel dispatch; I'd like a perf run on a 4k median context workload. if perf stable, i'm fine with 2h canary. @lee can you confirm platform telemetry hooks are enabled for per-model breakdown?

lee: confirmed — per-model and per-route latency + token counts are wired in staging. canary can push with our standard flag: `--canary-window=2h`. please include the collectd tag: `routing-fallback-v2`.

kyle: infra (kv/cache) quick check: this increases cache miss rate for models that get routed to new variants. estimate: ~8-12% extra hot-key churn for the first hour of rollout. we should bump the cache rehydrate concurrency to avoid spill. can you add this to the PR description so SRE can monitor?

jordan: added cache rehydrate note and suggested concurrency bump in PR body. thanks @kyle.

olivia: security check — I reviewed auth header ordering change in the earlier patch you referenced. main thing: make sure the signed headers list remains deterministic when we rewrite routing metadata. pls add a unit test asserting header ordering for a routed request. once that's in, I can greenlight.

jordan: will add unit test this afternoon.

sam: aside — if anyone on runtime wants to run my perf script locally: `./scripts/perf.sh --profile=4k --runs=5` (logs to /tmp/perf-*.json). I can share quick diff of median p50/p95 after runs.

lee: if we get runtime perf ok and olivia greenlights with the unit test, i can schedule the canary for Thu 10:00 PT. @deploy-bot can you reserve the window?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary window for PR #54231 — Thu 2026-03-19 10:00 PT, duration 2h, tag=routing-fallback-v2 — rolling deploy enabled. monitor dashboards: /dashboards/platform/routing, /dashboards/runtime/perf, /dashboards/infra/cache.

jordan: thanks all — i'll post when unit test and perf numbers are up. if anyone objects to timing, reply here; otherwise i'll merge post-canary if metrics look good. :thumbsup:
